transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-28 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Lucas Meyer (Redwood CSM), Marta Lopez (Solara VP Eng), David Chen (Solara SRE), Aisha Rahman (Solara CISO), Tommy Nguyen (Solara Platform)

Summary (auto): Postmortem review of 2026-05-21 latency/regression incident impacting Solara's inference pipeline; discussed root cause (KV cache eviction + model fallback mismatch), mitigations (patch, rollout plan), security/compliance questions, and next steps including benchmarks and follow-up runbook.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll try to keep to one hour, we wanted to walk through the postmortem, the immediate mitigations and next steps. Marta, do you want to kick us off with how this surfaced on your side?

[00:22] Marta: yeah thanks Jordan, so on Friday the 21st our customer facing chat started showing higher latency spikes and occasionally 5xxs, um it happened during a normal afternoon traffic burst, we saw about 12% error rate at the peak, like a basically degraded user experience.

[00:38] David: to add quick detail, our on-call pager fired at 14:04 UTC, we saw a bunch of long tail tokens, the Redwood inference nodes started falling back to the quantized variant which doesn't have the same sequence length prewarm, and the K V cache didn't have the prefixes because of a cache eviction storm.

[01:05] Priya: yeah from Redwood side we looked in the logs and observed an unexpected eviction pattern across a subset of Dedicated pool nodes. The eviction coincided with a spike in multi-turn sessions; some requests were routed to a model variant that lacked the same warm KV cache layout, so cold starts plus fallback created token blowouts.

[01:35] Tommy: sorry can I clarify, when you say fallback to quantized variant, was that an automatic policy? we didn't explicitly request quantization right now.

[01:45] Priya: good question, so the smart routing policy had a compatibility fallback enabled—when memory pressure rose we routed to a compatible smaller variant that was quantized. That path has reduced KV prefetch behavior, so it triggered additional token generation on the hot path.

[02:10] Marta: and the result was both higher latency and a couple of 5xxs because the runtime hit an unexpected OOM on a few nodes, so service degraded rather than graceful fallback.

[02:28] Lucas: quick note — customer impact timeline cross-referenced with our metrics: 14:02 to 14:27 was the major window, matched their 12% error rate, overall 0.8% of total requests saw >5s latency increase.

[02:45] Aisha: from a security/compliance lens we need to understand whether any request or customer data was logged in plaintext or routed through partner regions. Also want to confirm retention settings weren't changed during the incident.

[03:05] Jordan: yeah absolutely we'll include that in the postmortem. Priya, can you talk through root cause analysis?

[03:18] Priya: sure, tl;dr—primary root cause was workload induced KV cache eviction combined with automatic fallback to a quantized model variant that didn't share the same KV cache warm path. Secondary contributing factors: routing policy thresholds too aggressive, and an edge case in the runtime where simultaneous prefetch + eviction can race and cause OOMs on ~2% of nodes. There's also a small bug in our eviction bookkeeping where sequence length distribution stats were underreported.

[03:55] David: is this the same bookkeeping bug you rolled patch for in february? i thought that was fixed.

[04:03] Priya: so that patch fixed the common path but not the race condition when eviction happens concurrently with rebalancing. We missed that in the tests because the repro needs high multi-turn session concurrency.

[04:28] Marta: ok so what's the mitigation we can use right now? we had to route more traffic to their hosted endpoints but that's not sustainable.

[04:34] Jordan: immediate mitigation we pushed: we disabled the automatic fallback policy for your Dedicated pool and added a conservative routing threshold; second we deployed a hotfix to reduce the eviction aggressiveness and add extra prefetch guardrails.

[05:00] Priya: correct, the hotfix reduces eviction frequency by changing the LRU bucket window and also adds a safe-check so we won't fall back if the receiving variant lacks the required KV layout. That reduced incidents in canary by ~85% in our internal bench.

[05:22] Marta: we saw fewer errors after 18:00 on Friday, which aligns with your hotfix. but we need a long-term plan.

[05:30] Priya: long-term fixes: 1) runtime patch to eliminate the eviction/rebalance race, 2) better compatibility metadata between model variants so fallback only occurs when KV layouts match, 3) tighter tracing so we can correlate sequence length distributions in real-time, 4) a runbook for on-call to force-rollover or pin model versions during bursts.

[05:55] David: for SR, we also want a reproducible benchmark so we can validate at our scale — can you share the benchmark harness and the exact workload config you used for canary?

[06:10] Priya: yes we'll share the harness and the config. note that we used a multi-turn session profile derived from your production distribution, will provide seed scripts.

[06:28] Aisha: re: compliance — any of these changes affect encryption or logs? You mentioned extra tracing. We need assurance traces are stored with the same retention and encryption policies.

[06:42] Jordan: good point, tracing will be opt-in and stored under the same KMS keys; we won't change retention without written confirmation. We'll provide the SOC2 artifact and audit logs for the window.

[07:02] Marta: can you also clarify the SLA credit calculation? we saw a dip but not sure if it hits the SLA.

[07:09] Lucas: we are running the impact calc now; Jordan will share the draft with exact minutes affected and the projected credit under your contract.

[07:20] David: one more technical Q — is the KV cache global per modelloader or per instance? i got mixed info from earlier notes.

[07:30] Priya: it's per instance with cross-instance affinity for prefix sharing when requests are sticky, but we don't have a global prefix cache. the eviction happened on specific instances handling multi-turn sticky sessions.

[07:55] Tommy: does this imply we should move to a higher reserved memory profile to avoid eviction?

[08:00] Priya: yes that's an option — we can recommend increasing the memory profile for peak windows or configuring dedicated pins for heavy multi-turn routes. we'll provide estimated cost delta vs the risk.

[08:15] Marta: that cost delta would be key for the exec team, please include that in the follow-up.

[08:20] Jordan: noted. Priya, can you run through the rollout plan and verification steps?

[08:28] Priya: rollout plan: 1) push the non-racy eviction patch to canary (we did this in small canary 10% traffic), 2) run a 24h sustained bench with your session distribution, 3) if no regressions, push to 50% and run another bench for 8 hours, 4) full prod push with gradual traffic ramp and close monitoring. verification: tail latencies, OOM counts, and a few synthetic multi-turn checks.

[09:00] Marta: timeline estimate?

[09:03] Priya: we estimate patch plus canary bench in 1 week, broader canary in 2 weeks, full rollout 3 weeks assuming no regressions; we can accelerate if you approve a short maintenance window.

[09:20] Aisha: will the patch require node restarts or rolling restarts that could affect availability?

[09:28] Priya: rolling restarts will be needed for the runtime patch; we'll do controlled drain and health checks. downtime should be minimal but we'll coordinate windows.

[09:45] David: for the benchmarks, we'll run our own load against the canary endpoints; how do we coordinate tokens/credentials?

[09:55] Jordan: we'll provision a temporary key with scoped rate limits for your bench and share details in the follow-up.

[10:10] Marta: can we also get more detailed telemetry around the sequence length distribution? we want dashboards.

[10:18] Lucas: we'll add per-route seq-len histograms to the console and give you a dashboard link; expect that within the next week.

[10:30] Tommy: there was also a side question about data residency—some requests got routed through a different region during the incident?

[10:40] Jordan: we saw some cross-region failover for capacity reasons; we'll include exact routing logs in the artifacts. if you need strict residency we'll disable cross-region fallback for those routes.

[10:58] Aisha: please also include an enumeration of audit log entries for the incident window; we need to confirm no configuration changes were made externally.

[11:10] Priya: we'll export audit logs and include hashes; retention and encryption remain unchanged.

[11:28] Marta: ok let's recap actions and owners. Jordan?

[11:34] Jordan: sure — action items: 1) send full postmortem doc and raw logs (Jordan), 2) share benchmark harness and canary results (Priya), 3) customer to send precise on-call traces and a list of impacted customer accounts (David/Marta), 4) provide SOC2 artifact and confirm retention (Jordan/Lucas), 5) schedule runbook walkthrough (Lucas/Jordan). We'll put dates in the follow-up email.

[11:58] David: thanks everyone. small nit — in the postmortem please include exact request IDs for a sample failure so our SREs can cross reference.

[12:08] Jordan: will do. any final comments?

[12:12] Marta: no, thanks for the quick response and the hotfix.

[12:15] Aisha: thanks, please send compliance docs.

[12:18] Priya: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts by monday.

[12:22] Jordan: thanks, meeting adjourned.

End transcript.
